channel.title: Daily Recap — 💾 Apple News
channel.description: What happened in 💾 Apple News, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: First iPhone Duo reviews: polished, but heavy and missing Face ID
item.description:
The first full reviews of Apple's first foldable landed on launch day, and the consensus is strikingly consistent: the Duo is beautifully polished around the edges but rough in the middle. The Wall Street Journal's Nicole Nguyen found it wider, thicker, and heavier than a Pro iPhone — heavy enough that her hand hurt after extended one-handed use — while Marques Brownlee singled out the lack of Face ID as the biggest gripe.

Third-party apps that haven't been optimized for the foldable form factor drew complaints, though one reviewer stress-tested the hinge with an industrial robot through 10,000 open-close cycles. Early adopters seem undeterred: one day-one buyer calls it a wonder to use despite its quirks and plans to daily-drive it. The verdict so far is that this is a genuinely impressive first foldable with real first-generation trade-offs.

Sources

  • Daring Fireball: Nicole Nguyen’s Duo Review for the WSJ
  • Daring Fireball: MKBHD’s Duo Review
  • Daring Fireball: Tim Pan’s iPhone Duo Review
  • 9to5Mac: iPhone Duo one day later: Here’s why its quirks don’t make it any less incredible

item.title: Duo durability under scrutiny after broken screens and a failed stress test
item.description:
Launch day also brought the inevitable durability drama. A handful of early Duo units have shown up with broken inner screens, with Reddit reports pointing to a similar failure spot along the hinge and a bright line across the right side of the display. Separately, JerryRigEverything's torture test saw dust enter the hinge despite the phone's IP68 rating, overwhelming the magnets that hold it shut, before a bend test left a permanent green line and an unresponsive screen.

The important context: the problem doesn't appear widespread, and stores aren't reporting broken displays in meaningful numbers. The inner screen also only scratches at level 2 on the Mohs scale versus level 7 for the Ceramic Shield 2 outer screen — though its matte nano-texture coating makes marks appear to vanish. Worth watching, but not yet a launch crisis.

Sources

  • Daring Fireball: Marion Barry Meets the iPhone Duo
  • MacRumors: iPhone Duo Fails JerryRigEverything's Dusty Durability Test
  • AppleInsider News: YouTubers break the iPhone Duo, but stores aren't seeing broken displays

item.title: Teardowns reveal the Duo's two-battery design and 4,883 mAh total
item.description:
The first iPhone Duo teardowns are out, and they confirm the foldable splits its power across two cells: a larger 2,962 mAh battery and a smaller 1,921 mAh one, for a combined 4,883 mAh. Both cells can be removed with electrically-activated adhesive, a repairability-friendly touch.

The teardown breakdown also labels the logic board, which houses Apple's A20 Pro chip and C2 cellular modem, and shows the Touch ID sensor built into the side button — the Duo's substitute for Face ID. For a device this thin and hinge-constrained, splitting the battery across both halves is the engineering compromise that makes the whole design possible.

Sources

  • MacRumors: iPhone Duo Teardowns Reveal Two Batteries and More

item.title: Verizon apologizes for Duo pre-order delays; store pickup trickles back
item.description:
If you're still waiting on a Duo, you're not alone. Verizon emailed affected pre-order customers to apologize for an unexpected shipping delay, offering a $100 Verizon gift card usable toward bills or merchandise as compensation. The carrier didn't say how long the extra wait will be.

Meanwhile, Apple Store pickup reservations resumed in the U.S. and Canada early Saturday morning, but inventory is extremely limited — most stores had no pickup slots available at all. The pattern is familiar for a hot Apple launch: demand is outrunning supply in the first days, and patience (or a gift card) is the consolation prize.

item.title: Three Duo tips worth knowing: Touch ID, Apple Watch unlock, and volume buttons
item.description:
No Face ID means Duo owners are rediscovering Touch ID — and the community is already optimizing it. One owner's tip, now circulating widely, is to register the lowest segment of your index finger rather than the fingertip pad, since that part rests naturally against the side button as you pick the phone up, unlocking it in one motion.

If you wear an Apple Watch (Series 9 or later, Ultra 2 or later, or SE 3), you can skip the button entirely with Unlock with Apple Watch — the closest thing to a seamless Face ID experience on the Duo. And because the foldable gets rotated constantly, a Settings option remaps the volume buttons so the top or right button is always volume up. Small fixes, but they smooth over the Duo's biggest daily friction.

item.title: Apple teases 'Pro and Tell' event next week as iOS 27.2 nears release
item.description:
The Duo launch isn't the end of Apple's fall announcements. The company has teased a 'Pro and Tell' event for next week promising even more new products, keeping the launch parade rolling just days after its first foldable hit shelves.

Also on the near horizon: the public release of iOS 27.2 and related updates appears to be right around the corner. And in a smaller carrier-side twist this week, Verizon announced a hefty monthly charge for the iPhone Handoff feature that lets two iPhones share the same phone number — a reminder that the Duo era comes with new accessory and service costs.

Sources

item.title: Apple closes seven French stores ahead of fresh protests
item.description:
Seven Apple stores across France closed on Saturday as the country braced for another round of demonstrations, a week after looters targeted two of the company's locations. The closures include all three Paris stores — Champs-Élysées, Opéra, and Marché Saint-Germain — plus Bordeaux Sainte-Catherine, Lille, Strasbourg, and Aix-en-Provence.

The move looks precautionary: the seven locations all have entrances directly onto the street, making them harder to secure. It's a measure of how the unrest is spilling into everyday retail, with Apple choosing to protect employees and stores rather than risk a repeat of last week's looting.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Closes French Stores Ahead of Further Protests

item.title: Apple pushes back on DOJ bid for more evidence in antitrust case
item.description:
Apple and the U.S. Department of Justice are sparring over the scope of evidence in their antitrust case. The two sides had previously agreed to a June 20, 2025 cutoff for Apple's records, but with the evidence-gathering phase now running to late May 2027, DOJ lawyers want documents created up to 30 days before that deadline, arguing newer records could show whether the alleged anticompetitive practices are continuing.

Apple says expanding the search would delay the case by several months. The dispute is procedural, but it sets the tempo for one of the biggest antitrust fights in tech — and a longer discovery phase pushes any resolution further out.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Pushes Back on DOJ Request for More Evidence

item.title: iPhone Duo launch day brings back the lines — and the sellouts
item.description:
Apple's first foldable went on sale Friday, and launch-day lines — a ritual largely killed off by online pre-orders — returned in force. Dozens to hundreds of people queued at stores worldwide, some camping out days early, for a shot at the $1,999 device with its 5.4-inch outer display unfolding to 7.6 inches inside.

Supply is extremely tight: pre-orders slipped to January within 30 minutes of opening on October 16, and walk-in stock sold out fast. Store pickup reservations briefly resumed in Australia, China, Japan, and South Korea, but slots vanished almost immediately. In Austin, new CEO John Ternus — who took over in September — greeted the line himself, continuing the launch-day tradition in Tim Cook's absence.

item.title: Crackgate? Some Duo screens are breaking along the hinge on day one
item.description:
Hours after launch, Duo owners began posting photos of display cracks running along the hinge, most producing a line of bright pixels across one side of the screen. One Australian owner said his device cracked after fewer than 20 opens in about six hours, with no prior damage — he felt something catch around the internal hinge as he opened it.

It's early, and the scale is unclear: a handful of forum and Reddit reports don't yet make a widespread defect. But the hinge is the device's defining mechanism, so Apple will be under a microscope. The company also published Duo support documents today covering hinge troubleshooting, Touch ID, and cases, and released official DIY repair guides for the foldable.

item.title: First verdicts: a messy, expensive good time
item.description:
The review consensus is remarkably consistent: the Duo is genuinely fun and fresh, but compromised and buggy in first-generation ways. The Verge calls it a messy, expensive good time, noting the odd ritual of rotating the phone counterclockwise on opening so the cameras sit on top. Joanna Stern's review — which included a robot folding a unit 32,000 times in a week — lands on good, bad, and buggy, and she sorely missed Face ID.

Hands-on testers were more forgiving: AppleInsider found Apple had nearly solved its biggest form-factor concerns, and MacStories' first day, spent talking to Duo app developers in New York, felt like a slice of WWDC. The throughline is that the hardware delights while the software still catches up — a classic first-gen Apple story.

item.title: Living with the Duo: Pencil limits, split-screen pairs, and hidden tricks
item.description:
Day-one discoveries are filling in the Duo's practical picture. Only the $79 USB-C Apple Pencil works with it — Pencil 1, Pencil 2, and Pencil Pro are all incompatible. The foldable is also the first iPhone to run two apps side by side, with Split View on the inner display and the option to lock a pair so they always launch together.

Other findings: a hidden trick eases opening Control Center, developers are already shipping playful foldable apps (including a tiny retro Mac), and Apple is exploring ways to fix Safari's cramped layout on the narrow outer display. Perhaps most tellingly, the Duo ditches Face ID for a side-button Touch ID sensor, and owners can enable Rest Finger to Open to skip the swipe-up after unlocking.

item.title: The iPod turns 25 — and Apple hides a playable one on its website
item.description:
Twenty-five years to the day after Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPod on October 23, 2001, Apple is celebrating the device that put 1,000 songs in your pocket for $399 — and set the company on the path to the iPhone. Writers marked the anniversary by tracing how the iPod revived Apple, legitimized it with PC users, and reshaped the music industry before being eclipsed by the phone it made possible.

Apple's own tribute is a delight: the Apple Music website's 404 page now features a fully interactive first-generation iPod, complete with era-appropriate preloaded music, the correct click-wheel sounds, and even the secret Breakout game. Load a nonexistent Apple Music page in a browser to give it a spin.

item.title: iOS 27.1 is Duo-only; iOS 27.2 and watchOS 27.2 near the finish line
item.description:
Don't look for iOS 27.1 on your iPhone: the final release is exclusive to the Duo, which ships with it preinstalled and prompts a newer build with unspecified bug fixes during setup. Everyone else's next update is iOS 27.2, due next week, with no security fixes noted for the Duo-only build.

Meanwhile, Apple seeded a second watchOS 27.2 release candidate, four days after the first, ahead of next week's launch. The update brings new Siri AI features to the watch — including retained context from previous interactions, broader personal context, and faster responses — and extends Siri AI to more languages.

item.title: Next week's MacBook Pro promises a big redesign — with one catch
item.description:
Apple's fully redesigned MacBook Pro arrives next week, and 9to5Mac says it shapes up as a major upgrade — except in one key area, which the report leaves as the fly in the ointment. Details are still thin, but the framing suggests a machine that moves the Pro line forward substantially while asking buyers to accept a notable compromise.

Expect the full picture at next week's launch event, where the redesign will be judged against the current MacBook Pro lineup — and against the Duo's launch-week lesson that big redesigns rarely arrive without trade-offs.

item.title: Apple reclaims the world's most valuable company crown
item.description:
Wall Street liked Duo day: Apple retook the title of world's most valuable company from Nvidia on Friday, hitting new trading highs as the foldable launched. The rally capped a week of market-share gains on both sides of Apple's business.

In China, smartphone shipments fell 10% year over year in Q3 to a 14-year low, yet Apple gained ground as rising memory prices squeezed rivals. In PCs, Counterpoint estimates Mac shipments of 5.6 million units in Q3 — down 11% — but that beat a market that fell 21%, lifting Apple's share from 8.7% to 9.8%, with the MacBook Neo credited as a key contributor.

item.title: iPhone Duo launch day arrives amid "extraordinary" demand
item.description:
Friday, October 23 is launch day for Apple's first foldable, and Apple says demand is "nothing short of extraordinary." In a TechRadar interview, marketing SVP Greg Joswiak addressed in-store availability after a messy pre-order launch that saw delivery estimates slip within minutes of opening on October 16. First deliveries have begun in Australia and New Zealand, early pre-orders are marked "shipped," and buyers are lining up days early — though Apple warns retail stock will be limited, so many walk-ins will leave empty-handed.

Digitimes reports Apple boosted Duo orders roughly 44% (9.7M to 14M units over 12 months) on strong pre-orders — though AppleInsider cautions component orders don't equal shipments, especially with a complex hinge to manufacture at scale. Apple installed giant mirrored Duo displays at Fifth Avenue, Covent Garden, BKC in India, and Jing'an in Shanghai for the launch.

item.title: Reviews call it the best foldable ever — but apps are the weak link
item.description:
The embargo has lifted and the verdict is surprisingly unified: the iPhone Duo is the best foldable phone ever made, but this first generation comes with trade-offs. A MacRumors hands-on a day early found app support uneven — some apps fill the inner display, some (like Netflix with a half-fold mode) have Duo-specific features, and many un-updated apps sit in thick black bars. Apple's secrecy left most developers little time to prepare.

Apple is pushing back: it highlighted 50+ optimized apps with a "Made for iPhone Duo" App Store badge (apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later). Standouts include retro emulator Delta 2.0, with a Liquid Glass redesign and Nintendo DS layouts that span the crease, plus Apple's own GarageBand and TestFlight. A CT scan revealed the hinge locks anywhere from 15 to 145 degrees. Per John Gruber's updated review, the camera is terrific — nearly iPhone Air specs, just not iPhone 18 Pro caliber.

item.title: iPhone Duo 2 rumors: under-display Face ID and a bigger screen
item.description:
The first Duo hasn't hit shelves, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is already testing Duo 2 prototypes with Face ID beneath the outer display — fixing a key omission, since the first model uses side-button Touch ID like the iPad. The successor is expected next fall, though Apple reportedly hasn't finalized whether Face ID will ship.

Gurman also "heard" Apple is considering a slightly larger Duo, growing the inner display roughly half an inch from 7.6 to about 7.9–8.1 inches — a tweak, not a separate "Duo Max" — plus a possible telephoto camera. All of it signals confidence the foldable is a hit and investment in the next wave is already underway.

item.title: iWork gets an 'Intelligent Assistant' — then Apple briefly pulls the apps
item.description:
Apple rolled out AI-centric updates to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers, adding an "Intelligent Assistant" in beta for Creator Studio subscribers. In Numbers it builds formulas from natural language and generates tables; in Pages it drafts sections, adjusts tone, and generates images; in Keynote it assists with presentation creation. The update also adds Duo support and a new open Interchange Format (.keyx) for easier editing of Keynote files in other apps.

Then it got weird: shortly after the update landed, Apple temporarily removed all three apps from the App Store. It was unclear whether the removal was intentional or a bug, and Apple said nothing. The Mac versions have since returned (without the new update); the iOS versions hadn't reappeared as of reporting — an odd glitch for a suite at the center of Apple's AI push.

iOS 27.2 lands next week and it's shaping up to be meaningful. The standout is a new Phone app feature called Call Context, which one 9to5Mac editor calls an instant favorite — part of a broader iOS 27 wave across Notes, Wallet, Maps, and Messages. It also brings two new features for Apple TV subscribers, with details held until launch.

Beyond features, iOS 27.2 introduces design changes for select Apple apps. The timing — arriving just as the Duo goes on sale — suggests Apple wants the software story reinforcing the hardware launch, with Duo owners getting new features in the same week.

item.title: Apple blocks compromised certificates and warns of critical PHP flaws
item.description:
Two security stories dominated Apple's week. First, Apple blocked compromised certificates from certificate authority eMudhra that could have let attackers impersonate websites — Mozilla found their private keys were all numbers below 256, making them almost instantly recoverable. Apple pushed blocks to devices on October 19.

Second, critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618/109619) are being actively exploited against internet-exposed NAS devices, allowing code execution without login. PHP released patches for 8.2–8.5 on October 21; some site owners took sites offline preemptively, and not every NAS vendor has a fix — check for updates now. Separately, 9to5Mac argues Apple is finally delivering on Siri's AI promise just as expectations shift to agentic assistants, a race Apple says it won't sit out.

item.title: MacBook Neo cushions Apple as Q3 PC market slumps; event invites are out
item.description:
Counterpoint Research's Q3 2026 numbers show global PC shipments sliding, but Apple outperformed the broader market — with the MacBook Neo helping cushion the downturn. A bright spot in an otherwise gloomy quarter driven by rising component prices.

Attention now turns to next week's Apple "experience" in Los Angeles, teased as "Pro and tell." The headline act should be the first MacBook Pro redesign in five years — rumored to keep the M5 Pro/Max chips but add at least four exclusive advantages. Also rumored: an iPad mini with OLED screen, A20 chip, and improved speakers. Retailers are already clearing inventory — Amazon has the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro at a record-low $2,429 and $900 off the 36GB M5 Max model.

item.title: Appeals court upholds Apple's win in 'Servant' plagiarism lawsuit
item.description:
The Ninth Circuit upheld Apple's win in the long-running copyright fight over Apple TV thriller "Servant." Filmmaker Francesca Gregorini sued in January 2020, claiming the M. Night Shyamalan-produced series copied her film "The Truth About Emanuel." The case was dismissed, revived, then decided by a jury in Apple's favor early last year — and now the appeals court has maintained that ruling.

It's a meaningful win for Apple TV as the service keeps investing in originals. No twist ending here: the court agreed "Servant" wasn't a copy, closing one of the longest-running legal sagas around an Apple TV+ original.

item.title: iPhone Duo reviews: hardware impresses, software and biometrics lag
item.description:
Embargoed iPhone Duo reviews dropped Wednesday, two days before the October 23 launch: impressive hardware, visible rough edges. The hinge drew broad praise — Joanna Stern folded her unit over 32,000 times with a machine and found it essentially unchanged — and the crease is said to be nearly invisible. But reviewers flagged foldable realities: no Face ID, with Touch ID that reviewers call slow and jarring (Marques Brownlee says Apple built an intentional unlock delay into every press); a 4-megapixel under-display inner camera reviewers call washed out and “trash”; heat under load; the unfolded device tipping on some upright MagSafe stands; and unoptimized apps letterboxing with black bars. Bright spots Apple didn't announce: Edge Light, a virtual ring light for video calls, and a horizontal Reachability mode coming later this year.

John Gruber's bottom line: the Duo feels like an extraordinarily polished prototype rather than a finished product. Demand may not care — pre-orders sold out in moments, and Apple confirmed only extremely limited walk-in stock on Friday morning, so expect overnight lines.

item.title: Australia orders Apple to allow rival app stores by March 2027
item.description:
A Federal Court of Australia judge has ordered Apple to make sweeping, EU-style changes to its App Store rules by March 2027, capping a years-long antitrust battle with Epic Games. The 1,104-paragraph ruling finds Apple engaged in anticompetitive conduct and requires it to allow alternative app stores and end anti-steering practices that stop developers from pointing users to cheaper payment options.

The ruling imports Europe's Digital Markets Act playbook into Australian law, and it's the latest front in the global erosion of Apple's App Store control. Apple has confirmed it plans to appeal, so the deadline could shift — but the closed App Store model is losing ground in market after market.

Sources

item.title: Apple and DOJ deadlocked over documents in antitrust suit
item.description:
Apple and the US Department of Justice have filed a joint notice of impasse with the court over how recent Apple's documents must be to fall within discovery in the DOJ's ongoing antitrust lawsuit. The DOJ wants a broader, later cutoff — suspecting evidence from the past year could strengthen its case — while Apple argues the collection window is closed.

The case has run long enough that many original charges look increasingly stale, and this fight appears to be a last-ditch attempt to pull in fresher material. The court must now resolve the standoff, and the scope of internal documents the DOJ can see will shape whatever endgame the suit reaches.

Sources

item.title: Apple Music's “made by sound” rebrand goes live
item.description:
Apple officially rolled out its new Apple Music brand identity on Wednesday, now live on Apple's website. The red color scheme is gone, replaced by a black-and-white logo and app icon — and Apple says the visuals were literally “made by sound,” created by playing audio through a container of water and photographing the liquid rippling at the notes' frequencies.

The liquid-inspired look pairs with the Liquid Glass interface that debuted across Apple's platforms last year, part of a unified, fluid design language. Reaction has been mostly positive — Stephen Hackett calls it “literally liquid and glass,” aside from the missing color. It's a notable moment for a service that's never had a strong visual identity, arriving alongside Apple Music Hall's opening in Battersea, London.

item.title: iPhone Duo gains Apple Pencil support in iOS 27.2, plus Messages and iPadOS tweaks
item.description:
iOS 27.2's release candidate, expected publicly next week, brings Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo much earlier than Apple's original “before the end of 2026” promise. The USB-C Apple Pencil works on both the inner and outer displays for drawing, annotating, and scrolling, which makes the foldable a notably more credible productivity device — essentially an iPhone that docks into a small drawing tablet.

Elsewhere in the 27.2 betas, code points to a long-requested Messages option: excluding muted conversations from the unread badge count, so muted group chats stop hijacking your badge. iPadOS 27.2, meanwhile, picks up the Siri popup when selecting text, a recent Mac addition. Taken together, it's a meaningful first software update for the Duo that closes some of the gaps reviewers flagged this week.

item.title: Meta hit with record $25 billion penalty over Cambridge Analytica
item.description:
A New Mexico judge handed Meta a record-breaking $25 billion penalty on Wednesday over the Cambridge Analytica scandal, ruling the company responsible for 43 million violations of the state's consumer privacy laws after September's guilty finding at a two-week trial. Each violation carried a penalty of up to $5,000, and the court used them aggressively to reach the staggering total.

The judgment dwarfs even the FTC's previous $5 billion fine and signals that state-level privacy enforcement can carry real financial teeth. Expect Meta to appeal — and expect other state attorneys general to take notes. For Apple-watchers, the case lands as another data point in the broader industry reckoning over data collection practices that Apple has been positioning itself against for years.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent
item.description:
Anthropic on Wednesday introduced Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that “reaches out before you ask” — connecting to your apps to surface things that need attention and completing tasks in the cloud without local access to your computer. It runs in a virtual machine with its own browser, like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, and targets busy professionals and small business owners: it tracks email and calendars and keeps working even when the app is closed.

The launch completes the trio of major proactive agents from the leading AI labs, shifting the frontier from chatbots you consult to agents that act on your behalf. The open questions are the same ones dogging the category: how much access users will grant, and how reliably these agents handle real tasks unsupervised.

Slow Horses has quietly become one of the streamer's most reliable critical hits, anchored by Gary Oldman's Slough House crew of disgraced MI5 agents, and the quick renewal-plus-trailer turnaround suggests Apple knows exactly which originals are carrying its prestige-TV brand.

item.title: iPhone Duo launches Friday — order limits, first unboxing, and Samsung's foldable counterattack
item.description:
The iPhone Duo goes on sale this Friday, October 23, and the week leading up to launch is unfolding like a case study in supply-constrained demand. The first unboxing video from outside the press has surfaced, showing the device ships flat rather than folded and is otherwise packaged like any other iPhone. Reviews are expected tomorrow, and leaked App Store screenshots of Apple's built-in apps on the Duo show iPad-like landscape interfaces with sidebar navigation — a first real look at day-to-day use.

Demand is clearly straining supply: Apple is limiting orders to two per customer in the US, UK, and elsewhere after shipping dates slipped into January within minutes of pre-orders opening, an explicit move against scalpers. And Samsung is reportedly spooked, with plans to launch six different foldable phones next year in an attempt to counter the Duo — even before Apple's device has shipped a single unit to a customer.

item.title: Apple deepens US manufacturing push with titanium, camera deals and Houston Mac mini assembly
item.description:
Apple is making its most aggressive case yet for domestic manufacturing. The company announced new and expanded American Manufacturing Program partnerships: up to $100 million over three years to Pennsylvania-based Perryman, which produces the titanium used in iPhone Duo enclosures, and an extended deal with Delaware-based Qnity Electronics to make advanced films for the variable aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro. All told, Apple says nearly 100 components across the two phones are produced by American companies in more than a dozen states.

Apple reiterated that Mac mini assembly in the US will begin later this year, with Foxconn building the computers in Houston, Texas; US-assembled units will primarily serve the US market. The announcements fit Apple's broader pledge to invest in domestic manufacturing.

item.title: Taction wants more money after record $5.7 billion patent verdict against Apple
item.description:
The record-breaking $5.7 billion jury verdict against Apple may not be the end of the story. Taction Technology is asking a federal judge to award hundreds of millions more, arguing the September verdict only covers sales from 2021 through late March 2026 — and that Apple also owes prejudgment interest plus royalties on future sales.

The jury found that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed two Taction patents covering haptic feedback — the taps and vibrations in devices — though the infringement was not found to be willful. Apple disputes the verdict entirely and is seeking to have it overturned or to get a new trial. If the award stands, it would be among the largest patent verdicts in history, and ongoing royalties would turn a one-time penalty into a continuing cost on every iPhone and Apple Watch sold.

It runs on Qwen 3.6 or Perplexity's post-trained PPLX Pro in the Perplexity app for Mac on supported Apple silicon machines, with code and tool execution isolated in sandboxes, and it can operate native Mac apps. The local mode, available to Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers, complements September's Hybrid Compute update.

item.title: HomeView was ready for years — it just had to wait for Siri AI
item.description:
Apple's $299 HomeView home hub was reportedly mostly finished for years, kept in limbo while the company waited on Siri AI. Now that both are out, Apple executives are framing the delay as necessary: the new Siri AI is the "magic" of HomeView, in the words of VP of product marketing Kaiann Drance, but its power is in how little users have to interact with it.

The killer features, Apple says, are simplicity and an assistant good enough to stay in the background — the device "comes together in a way that we haven't been able to deliver before," per Drance. It's a revealing explanation for the long-rumored device's endless delays, and a bet that an AI assistant, not another screen, is the missing piece of the smart-home hub.

On the hardware side, the new fourth-generation Apple TV 4K can connect to up to four HomePods in front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right positions for an all-Apple surround sound system — and a quieter new feature, Whole Room Audio, spreads sound evenly across the four speakers for parties or game day. item.title: UK regulator says Apple's NFC opening still doesn't let Apple Pay rivals compete
item.description:
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority says Apple's concessions on iPhone NFC access still don't make it practical for developers to build genuine Apple Pay competitors. Despite Apple loosening its grip on the NFC chip under EU pressure, the CMA says developers report that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions are holding up wider third-party adoption — the same complaints that followed Apple's 2024 investigation into digital wallets and its European agreement.

The UK is now pushing for easier access at no cost for its own developers, arguing that simply mirroring the EU's terms won't cut it. It's the latest sign that regulators are treating Apple's payment chip as infrastructure that should be open — and that the compromises Apple struck in Europe are becoming a floor, not a ceiling, for what watchdogs demand elsewhere.

item.title: iPhone Duo Launch: Capped Orders, No Walk-Ins, Shifting Delivery Dates

Apple is limiting U.S. customers to two Duos per order, and in Japan and South Korea the Duo and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be reservation-only pickups — no walk-ins at launch, a mix of supply constraints and Apple's usual anti-scalping posture in Asia. Apple told outlets pre-order demand was "extraordinary," with stock selling out in moments amid manufacturing issues, so Apple Stores are expected to have little or no inventory on day one.

There is some relief: customers whose orders initially showed January delivery dates are seeing them bumped up, with some U.S. and Japanese pre-orders moving into a November 20–30 window. And one mystery is settled: an EU regulatory filing pegs the Duo's dual-battery capacity at 4,883 mAh, between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max — though real-world tests already showed battery life on par with the 18 Pro.

item.title: Apple Acquires AI Audio Startup Samplab
item.description:
Apple quietly acquired Samplab, a Zurich-based AI audio editing company, back in June — revealed only now through a European Commission acquisitions filing. The deal covers certain assets and hires of Samplab employees, echoing Apple's similar arrangement with podcast AI firm Huxe. Samplab's tools convert audio to MIDI, detect and edit chords, split songs into stems, and edit individual notes within polyphonic audio without altering the original timbre.

The likely destination is Logic Pro and GarageBand. Logic already has Stem Splitter and Chord ID, but polyphonic note editing would be genuinely new — a meaningful creative upgrade for musicians working inside Apple's pro audio tools. Expect the technology to surface gradually in future Logic Pro releases rather than as a standalone announcement.

Apple's first foldable iPhone is a genuine smash, and a genuine supply-chain mess.
